info.name: Sanad App — Chat
info.description: Authenticated Chat Lane A surface (frozen contract endpoints 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10): conversation list/open-or-get, attachment upload/serve, read marks, block/unblock/list, and per-user hiding. Use Sanad.local.postman_environment.json and supply a disposable access token in the accessToken collection variable; set recipientUserId to a second disposable user. Messages, unread counts, reports, and the admin queue (endpoints 3-4, 8, 11-15) arrive with Lane B. Requests, bodies, and response examples are statically authored from the verified controller/handler behavior and docs/chat/reports/lane-a-*.md — they were never executed against a live API or database, and no secrets are stored here.

item.name: 01. Conversations
item.description: Endpoints 1 and 2. All routes resolve the participant from the JWT (401 without a token); unknown, foreign, and ineligible ids answer the same generic privacy 404.

request.description: Endpoint 1 → 200 PagedResult {items, page, pageSize, totalCount, totalPages}, ordered by lastActivityOnUtc descending. page is clamped up to 1; pageSize is clamped to 1–100 (default 20). Only the caller's conversations appear, minus rows the caller hid; foreign rows are never an error. participant is always the other side of the pair (Identity display name, English preferred with Arabic fallback; avatarUrl may be null). Lane A stub: lastMessage is null and unreadCount is 0 until Lane B owns messages. 401 without a token.

response.name: 200 — Page of conversations (Lane A stub fields)

request.description: Endpoint 2 → always 200, never a duplicate: created=true means new history; created=false returns the existing row for the same normalized pair + booking reference (and reopens it for this caller only if this caller had hidden it — the peer's hidden flag and lastActivityOnUtc stay untouched). bookingId null = direct scope; replace null with a booking GUID for booking-scoped chat (a booking-scoped row and a direct row between the same pair are different conversations). Self-open, unknown/deleted recipient, empty recipient id, and a Guid.Empty booking reference all collapse into the same generic 404 Chat.Conversation.NotFound. Not yet checked (documented TODO seam): the role/participant matrix from docs/chat/plan.md and booking state (both users on a non-cancelled, non-expired booking) — a booking id is currently stored as-is.

  "type": "https://httpstatuses.com/404",

  "detail": "The requested resource was not found.",

item.name: 02. Attachments
item.description: Endpoints 5 and 6. Conversation-scoped, uploader-bound uploads in private storage; serving is controller-authorised and participant-only.

request.description: Endpoint 5 → 201 {attachmentId, fileName, contentType, sizeBytes}; fileName is the sanitized echo of the original name (last path segment, fallback "file") while storage uses a generated safe key. multipart/form-data with a single file field is required (415 otherwise). Limits by declared type: image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp ≤ 5 MB (5,242,880); video/mp4 ≤ 50 MB (52,428,800); application/pdf ≤ 10 MB (10,485,760) — documents are PDF-only in Lane A, no voice notes. Magic bytes are verified against the declared type (a matching content type alone is never trusted). Errors: 400 Chat.Attachment.Invalid (missing/empty file, length mismatch, signature mismatch, persistence failure), 400 Chat.Attachment.TooLarge, 400 Chat.Attachment.UnsupportedType; 404 generic privacy (Chat.Conversation.NotFound) when the conversation id is unknown or the caller is not a participant — that gate runs before file validation; the host also caps the whole request at 50 MB (413/connection reset). Uploads are created unbound and bind to a single message when Lane B's send path runs. Select a local file before sending.

request.description: Endpoint 6 → 200 raw bytes with the stored content type plus Cache-Control: no-store and Pragma: no-cache. Participant-only: unknown conversation, foreign caller, unknown attachment id, an attachment owned by a different conversation, and a missing blob all return the identical generic 404 (Chat.Attachment.NotFound), so the caller cannot tell which check failed. No signed URLs exist in V1; 401 without a token.

item.name: 03. Read state
item.description: Endpoint 7. Per-user read watermark recorded verbatim; unread counts and read ticks are Lane B's to interpret.

request.description: Endpoint 7 → 204, idempotent: one row per (conversation, user), so repeats update the same row and refresh its ReadOnUtc stamp. The message id is recorded verbatim — Lane A has no Message table, so any non-empty GUID is accepted and Lane B interprets marks (unread counts, read ticks); set lastReadMessageId to a real message id once Lane B exists. Errors: 400 Chat.ConversationRead.Invalid for a participant sending the empty GUID 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 or an omitted lastReadMessageId property; a non-GUID or missing body never reaches the handler (generic model-binding 400, no Chat code); the generic privacy 404 for unknown/foreign conversations runs before payload validation, so a malformed body is never an existence oracle. A read mark never changes lastActivityOnUtc, hiding, or visibility, and survives hide/reopen.

item.name: 04. Blocks
item.description: Endpoint 9. Per-user, directional blocks. Block state is not consulted by any Lane A route; Lane B enforces it at send time with the generic non-participant failure.

request.description: Endpoint 9 → 204, idempotent (a repeated block of the same user succeeds again; the unique pair index is the database backstop). Directional: the (blocker, blocked) row denies sends FROM the blocked user TO the blocker at Lane B send time, while the blocker may still send. Errors: 400 Chat.Block.Invalid for self-block or an empty/absent blockedUserId; the generic privacy 404 (Chat.Block.NotFound) when the target id is not registered, so this route can never probe whether an arbitrary user id exists. Blocking changes nothing about conversations today (list, open, read, hide, upload, serve are unaffected).

request.description: Endpoint 9 → always 204, idempotent: a missing row still succeeds, so unblock never reveals whether a block ever existed. Removing the row is the complete Lane B off-switch — send-time checks read the block rows directly, so unblocking restores sending. 401 without a token.

response.name: 204 — Unblock succeeded (also when no block existed)

request.description: Endpoint 9 → 200 array of the caller's own blocked user ids, most-recent block first (CreatedOnUtc descending). Per-user isolation: ids blocked by anyone else are never listed.

response.name: 200 — Caller's blocked user ids (most recent first)

item.name: 05. Hide conversation
item.description: Endpoint 10. Hide is a per-user visibility flag, not a delete — the peer keeps the history and nothing is erased.

request.description: Endpoint 10 → 204, idempotent for participants. The row disappears from this caller's GET conversations list while the other party keeps it and its full history; nothing is erased (there is no erasure path in V1, retention is indefinite). Hiding is not activity: lastActivityOnUtc, read marks, and the peer's view are untouched. Reopen by calling "Open or get conversation" again for the same pair (+ booking) — that returns created:false and unhides the caller only. Unknown or foreign conversation ids answer the generic privacy 404. 401 without a token.
